source.name: Amoeboid

source.name: Bladerager Troll
sourceDistinctions: Printed p. 4 gives explicit ECL and numeric LA. On p. 6 the introduction describes the class-level heading as advancement for creatures unsuitable for player use. The glossary on p. 213 defines numeric LA for player characters or cohorts. Treat the profile as a DM-approved monster conversion. The NPC follows the printed class advancement.
The original two-page entry describes the operation that makes a troll into this subtype. The catalog groups this source-defined operation under Troll.
Fighter 1 adds +1 BAB, +2 base Fort, 1 rank in Intimidate and Weapon Focus (claw) as its fighter bonus feat. HP is printed 81 plus a 5 on the fighter die and +9 Constitution.

The death burst stays DC 22. The large giant attack math is BAB 5, Strength +9, size −1, Weapon Focus +1 for the claws and Multiattack −2 for the bite. Power Attack applies to the natural weapon hits.

sourceDistinctions: The original entry lists +4 LA and calls briarvexes generally unsuitable as PCs. Saltburr is built as a classed NPC.
Druid spells do not stack with the racial entangle. CR 6 is an encounter estimate using a nonassociated first class level. The class Hit Die has a recorded roll of 5.

entries.name: Canomorph

source.name: Canomorph
sourceDistinctions: Haraknin combines the original 3.0 hell hound racial scores with the printed Canomorph rules and changes the example’s barbarian to ranger to respect lawful alignment. Its sample scimitar damage die conflicts with the 3.0 equipment table. The NPC uses the equipment table’s 1d6.

The Vultivor character paragraph sends readers to the vorr on p. 186. That species uses racial d8s. The Vultivor example on pp. 28–29 has d10s and an extended Shadow Jump allowance. Both source values are retained with their respective scope.
The common Command Fiendish Hound entry lacks a caster level and DC. The build sets CL to five total Hit Dice for this ability and uses Charisma and the cleric spell level for DC 12.

sourceDistinctions: Yugoloth is the original source grouping. No parentSpecies link is used for this catalog entry.

The book’s classed assassin example confirms that curse caster level and both racial save DCs key off total HD. The rogue class Hit Die has a recorded roll of 4. The +1 Dexterity increase at 8 HD is included in all affected numbers.

sourceDistinctions: The build uses the epic racial chassis with zero class levels, the printed racial base attack and saves, and original feat choices. Its aberration type follows the printed stat block.
For the 20-ft. aura, the 24-hour immunity from a successful Will save is applied to that foe’s movement save. The teleportation descriptor suppression remains an area effect.
Ethereal Bore uses the printed shift cadence in both directions. The linked spell supplies ethereal movement and maximum duration.

entries.name: Ethergaunt
entries.aliases: Ethergaunt / khen-zai. Keep red, white and black forms together.

source.name: Ethergaunt
sourceDistinctions: The dedicated player section gives the ECL increments and expressly stacks wizard levels with innate spellcasting. The red has innate Wizard 9 casting plus one actual Wizard level. The build adds the saves and skills of one class level only.

The text says ethergaunts cannot speak and still lists spells with verbal components. The worked NPC prepares Silent Spell versions in raised slots so a special verbal-component exception is unnecessary.
The portrait shows a normally closed mask. Its oval faceplate, central seam and trailing flesh tendrils identify the red caste at thumbnail size.

source.name: Fensir
sourceDistinctions: Rakka appears in its own stat block under Fensir and has a dedicated character paragraph. The worked NPC is an ordinary Fensir and uses the printed wizard stacking rule.

Source numbers for ordinary and Rakka rock attacks include inconsistencies. The example independently adds the racial +1, size modifier, Dexterity and BAB. Point Blank Shot applies when the target is within 30 ft.

source.name: Geppettin
source.heading: Bisque Traits, Marionette Traits and Plushie Traits
source.sourceDistinctions: The v1.4 Marionette chooses Small or Medium and has 30-ft. walking speed. Use the non-Two-Handed restriction and the on-turn attack timing for Clipped Strings. Brass Pin uses Small and a shield. Chapter 1 p. 11 gives general language choices.

entries.name: Gillfolk
entries.publication: Book of Heroic Races: Player Races 2
entries.aliases: Gillfolk. Shoreline and deep-sea Gillfolk share one claim. Keep Merrow, Merfolk and Pathfinder Gillmen separate.

source.name: Gillfolk
source.publication: Book of Heroic Races: Player Races 2
source.sourceLocator: Gillfolk Racial Traits, Deep Sea Gillfolk and Shore Line Gillfolk
source.sourceDistinctions: The 2017 publisher preview contains printed pp. 1–3. Page 1 identifies Gillfolk and the open-content license covers racial traits and subraces. The preview stops before the Gillfolk trait folios, which remain unverified. The attributed Open Gaming Network trait section explicitly gives Medium size. Its introductory copy contains unrelated text and is not used to infer traits. The build reads advantage against cold as advantage on relevant saving throws. It applies disadvantage from Water Born to eligible action rolls, not saving throws.

entries.name: Greenspawn Zealot
entries.aliases: Greenspawn Zealot. Keep other spawn of Tiamat outside this profile.

source.name: Greenspawn Zealot
sourceDistinctions: Printed p. 4 gives explicit ECL and numeric LA. On p. 6 the introduction describes the class-level heading as advancement for creatures unsuitable for player use. The glossary on p. 213 defines numeric LA for player characters or cohorts. Treat the profile as a DM-approved monster conversion. The NPC follows the printed class advancement.
This claim uses the green-scaled chaplain in Monster Manual V. Earlier green dragonspawn such as the greenspawn sneak are different entries.

The build adds cleric 1 to the printed typical specimen. The class contributes +2 Fort and Will base saves and 2 Concentration ranks. Hit points are printed 45 plus a 4 on the cleric die and +3 Constitution. The evil domain slot uses protection from good and spontaneous inflict conversion excludes that slot.
The source prints the 18-point touch pool. The example adds no class-based pool scaling. The supernatural touch save remains 10 + 3 + 3 = 16 with this build.

The score for Strength is absent. The original creature has no Strength score, and no substitute score is assumed.

entries.name: Keeper
entries.aliases: Keeper. Use the Fiend Folio creature and its character rules.

source.name: Keeper
sourceDistinctions: The PC example and the stat block agree. Four racial HD plus LA +3 and one class level give ECL 8.
The April printing lists generic outsider darkvision and also specifically describes the species as blind and reliant on sonar. The NPC uses the more specific sensory description.
One mimic weapon attacks once despite BAB or class progression. With two weapons, keep the printed secondary attack penalty and off-hand damage.

entries.name: Kesh
entries.aliases: Kesh. Use the Esper Genesis printing.

source.name: Kesh

source.sourceDistinctions: Specialist pp. 97–99, standard language options p. 114, Pilot p. 122, armor p. 132, weapons p. 135, tools p. 142, alter appearance pp. 214–215, shared vision pp. 258–259. Minor Alteration does not give a channeling ability. The sample NPC uses Charisma as a table ruling, following the same species’ explicit Memory Meld ability.

entries.name: Mandrake
entries.aliases: Plantfolk player rules. Keep Demonthorn Mandrake and Piney separate.

source.name: Mandrake
source.heading: Mandrake Traits, Entangling Vines and Creating Your Character
source.sourceDistinctions: Autumn is a 3rd-level vine effect in v1.4. Alder treats the second creature as otherwise eligible under the printed targeting rules. Shillelagh targets a limb and its other material ingredients stay in use. Armor is purchased gear.

source.sourceDistinctions: Warrior pp. 103–105, Soldier p. 126, armor p. 132, greataxe p. 135. The introductory fiction depicts a Stonefang’s power axe. This NPC uses the printed greataxe mechanics for its illustrated axe.

entries.name: Mohrg
entries.publication: Libris Mortis: The Book of Undead (2004)
entries.aliases: Mohrg. Use the printed monster-class progression.

source.name: Mohrg
source.publication: Libris Mortis: The Book of Undead (2004)
source.page: pp. 36–37, Table 2–4 and Mohrg class features
sourceDistinctions: The printed slams, improved grab and tongue timing are from the monster class. The base progression has one slam and the level 12 build has no spawn feature.

Uses the Human bonus feat and skill point rules, retaining applicable Human features per Libris Mortis p. 34. Human skill benefits are applied on HD-bearing levels only. The two ordinary score increases use the 4th and 8th Hit Dice and both go to Strength.

The article gives no duration beyond using minor illusion and concentrating, so this build uses the cantrip’s one-minute cap. The Hallucination Spores DC is Intelligence-based, and Pacifying Spores use a printed fixed DC 11. These are the standalone traits, separate from the monster stat block.

entries.name: Rilmani
entries.aliases: Rilmani. Keep Ferrumach, Cuprilach and Aurumach forms together.

source.name: Rilmani
sourceDistinctions: The player paragraph begins on p. 140 and ends on p. 141. The Ferrumach, Cuprilach and Aurumach printed Hit Dice and level adjustments agree with the three player ECL offsets.
Tarsen retains the printed equipment and adds Weapon Focus (battleaxe) from fighter 1 and Improved Initiative at total HD 9.
The Ferrumach action list uses its CL 9 spell-like abilities and preserves CL 10 for the fear aura.

entries.name: Shaedling
entries.aliases: Shaedling. Keep Shade and Shadow Fey separate.

source.name: Shaedling
sourceDistinctions: Printed p. 4 gives explicit ECL and numeric LA. On p. 6 the introduction describes the class-level heading as advancement for creatures unsuitable for player use. The glossary on p. 213 defines numeric LA for player characters or cohorts. Treat the profile as a DM-approved monster conversion. The NPC follows the printed class advancement.

The stat block on p. 148 limits Sleeping Curse to its struck target. A Lore result mentions secondary victims, but supplies no procedure. The build uses the stat-block rule. Javelin damage uses the normal gossamer javelin in this encounter.

p. 148 does not state Wall of Darkness height, placement range or duration. The example sets these at 10 ft., 30 ft. and 5 rounds for table use. Standard action follows the normal supernatural action rule.

The printed typical specimen has three named feats at four racial Hit Dice without designating a bonus feat. The NPC retains the listed feats. Rogue 1 adds +2 base Reflex, 9 skill ranks, trapfinding and sneak attack. The selected ranks are Hide +1, Move Silently +1, Listen +3, Spot +3 and Tumble +1. HP is printed 22 plus a 4 on the class die and +2 Constitution.

source.sourceDistinctions: v1.4 gives 120-ft. Ethereal Vision on the Material Plane, baseline Spirit Speech with proficiency-bonus questions, and the listed exceptions and movement thresholds. Chapter 1 p. 11 gives general language choices. Mira knows no spell slots.

entries.publication: Book of Heroic Races: Player Races 1 (2015)
entries.aliases: Tengu / Tengus. Use Jon Brazer’s version. Keep Kenku, Ravenfolk and Pathfinder Tengu separate.

source.name: Tengu
source.publication: Book of Heroic Races: Player Races 1 (2015)
source.sourceLocator: Tengu Traits, Cosmopolitan Tengus and Nomadic Tengus
source.sourceDistinctions: The 2015 publisher preview stops at printed p. 6, with Tengu named on p. 1 and the trait folios outside the preview. Despite its name, the reprinted Gifted Linguist grants an artisan's-tools proficiency for a single daily check. Pell uses Cosmopolitan.

entries.name: Ushemoi
entries.aliases: Ushemoi. Keep Arkamoi, Hadrimoi, Lashemoi and Turlemoi together.

source.name: Ushemoi
sourceDistinctions: Printed p. 4 gives explicit ECL and numeric LA. On p. 6 the introduction describes the class-level heading as advancement for creatures unsuitable for player use. The glossary on p. 213 defines numeric LA for player characters or cohorts. Treat the profile as a DM-approved monster conversion. The NPC follows the printed class advancement.

Core claim groups all four printed Ushemoi forms. The Hadrimoi DR uses “and” in its stat block while the other forms either have no such distinction or use “or”. The Turlemoi stat block places Rising Courage on its immunity line. The ability text clarifies the immunity requires a +3 attack bonus from Strength from Pain.

Barbarian 1 adds +1 BAB, +2 base Fort, one Listen rank and 10 ft. fast movement. At total HD 3, take Toughness for +3 HP. HP is printed 15 plus a 7 on the class die, +3 Constitution and +3 Toughness. Rage adds 2 HP per Hit Die for a total of 6 temporary increase to current and maximum HP, lost when rage ends.
Toughness is the normal 3 HD feat. Rage rounds are 3 plus the improved +5 Constitution modifier. The pain steps and rage do not change the listed level adjustment.

sourceDistinctions: The printed Cleric 1 example is expressly ECL 29. The three values are 22 racial HD, one class level and LA +6.
The class has one level. The racial +16 BAB and racial saves remain. Cleric 1 provides +0 BAB, +2 Fortitude and Will, one d8 and the usual class spell resources.

The April book’s racial spell list prints baleful polymorph. The build leaves the transitional list intact and uses the listed natural attacks, which are independent of the stat block’s printed weapon iteratives.
The divine focus is ordinary. The optional p. 195 serpent symbol magic item grants an extra ability this build does not carry.

sourceDistinctions: The fighter level adds +1 BAB, +2 Fortitude and Weapon Focus (longspear). Total 9 HD also adds Improved Initiative. The four fighter skill points add two ranks each to Climb and Intimidate.
The stated hit points use the printed 68 HP plus a 6 on the fighter Hit Die and +4 Constitution. Warping Energy rounds down from 9 total Hit Dice for 4d6, then adds +2 Intelligence.

The creature entry treats warping energy as a normal attack and gives no touch designation. The printed ranged +12 matches the base attack, Dexterity and Weapon Focus outside Point Blank Shot range. SR stays at 18 because the entry gives a fixed value.
